measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this proposed constitutional school-system merger process.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Create the multi-county school-system merger process, including the impact study and voter-approval requirements after a qualifying protest.
measureRecords.whatItDoes: Amendment 2 would add a process to the Alabama Constitution for merging two or more neighboring county boards of education into one multi-county school system. Before a merger could occur, the State Board of Education would have to study the proposed merger and publish the study before the merger could be finalized. If at least 25 percent of the qualified voters in any affected county school system submit a written protest, the merger could not take effect unless a majority of the voters in each affected county approve it at the next general election, along with an overall majority of the votes cast in all the affected counties. The amendment would also require the State Board of Education to adopt rules to implement the merger process.

measureRecords.noMeans: Reject these proposed constitutional requirements for school-board policies on the Pledge and prayer.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Require local school-board policies for the daily Pledge of Allegiance and student-led prayer, with the stated rights not to participate.
measureRecords.whatItDoes: Amendment 3 would change the Alabama Constitution to require each local board of education to adopt a policy requiring each public K-12 school to conduct the Pledge of Allegiance to the United States flag at the beginning of each school day. It would also require each local board to adopt a policy allowing student-initiated and student-led prayer in public K-12 schools. No student could be required to participate in the prayer, and students would have the right to opt out of the Pledge or the prayer based on their own beliefs.

measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this proposed constitutional requirement for national anthem policies in public schools.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Require local school-board policies for the weekly national anthem broadcast or an approved live performance of the first stanza.
measureRecords.whatItDoes: Amendment 4 would change the Alabama Constitution to require local boards of education to adopt policies about The Star-Spangled Banner in public K-12 schools. Each policy would require the school to broadcast the first stanza at least once each week during school hours. A local board could instead allow a school-approved band, choir, vocal group, or vocalist to perform the first stanza during school hours, using the version archived by the Library of Congress.
